title: Video Stitching
summary: Given video clips of a sporting event lasting time seconds, each described by start and end times, determine the minimum number of clips needed to cover the entire event by cutting them into segments.
statement: Given video clips of a sporting event lasting time seconds, each described by start and end times, determine the minimum number of clips needed to cover the entire event by cutting them into segments. If coverage is impossible, return -1.
constraints: Clips have integer endpoints and target time is positive.
Return the fewest clips covering every instant from zero through time, or -1.
reference_solution:
def minimum_video_clips(clips, time):
 clips.sort();used=0;covered=0;at=0
 while covered<time:
  farthest=covered
  while at<len(clips) and clips[at][0]<=covered:farthest=max(farthest,clips[at][1]);at+=1
  if farthest==covered:return -1
  covered=farthest;used+=1
 return used

def minimum_video_clips(clips, time):
 clips.sort();used=0;covered=0;at=0
 while covered<time:
  farthest=covered
  while at<len(clips) and clips[at][0]<=covered:farthest=farthest if farthest>covered else clips[at][1];at+=1
  if farthest==covered:return -1
  covered=farthest;used+=1
 return used
hints: At each boundary, any next clip must start no later than current coverage.
Among all such clips, extend to the farthest end.
Sort by start, scan all currently available clips, commit one extension, and repeat.
Choosing a shorter available extension can never reduce the clips needed later.
